passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Chaptered text prints the operative expansion but names no legislator.
House Third Reading final passage of a single-subject ESA bill, 26 of 60 members against, so not near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: She co-sponsored and voted Aye on HB2853 (2022), whose new section 15-2401.01 makes "qualified student" include any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in "A kindergarten program" or "Any of grades one through twelve", while section 15-2402 transfers the monies that would otherwise go to the student's district into the account for "Tuition or fees at a qualified school". That is the rung "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family", not "Expanding voucher eligibility to most families", because the enacted eligibility is all public-school-eligible students rather than most.
